headline: Sell Atlanta first, the Hawks second: city codes, the MLK night, and taste doors at the rink, the AUC and the barbershop.

archetype.name: The Culture Capital's Swing Fans
archetype.description: A Black-led, metro-wide crowd that treats the arena as a runway and Atlanta itself as the team; loyal in spirit, loud only when the night means something (MLK Day, a Cup Friday, a playoff series).

pulse.teamMoment: Jalen Johnson's Hawks (46-36, No. 6 seed, lost 4-2 to the champion Knicks after leading 2-1) reloaded around defense under Quin Snyder with No. 8 pick Kingston Flemings, Lu Dort, Ryan Nembhard, Aaron Wiggins and Devin Carter, while 2024 No. 1 pick Zaccharie Risacher went to Dallas.

verifiedMoment: Jalen Johnson's Hawks reloaded around defense after a 6-seed season: No. 8 pick Kingston Flemings, plus trades for Lu Dort, Ryan Nembhard, Aaron Wiggins and Devin Carter, with 2024 No. 1 pick Zaccharie Risacher shipped to Dallas.

scorecard.rationale: Atlanta has one of the league's deepest design wells (Black Mecca, hip-hop, HBCU, rink and car culture) and a big, style-literate metro, but Hawks fandom runs below the city's cultural heat and arrives in spikes. Retail is broad yet car-dependent and mall-split, with taste set in small independent doors.

headline: Boston backs the banners while it doubts the roster: sell heritage, winter and neighborhoods, not players.

archetype.name: The Banner Counters
archetype.description: A multigenerational fan base that measures itself in titles and treats Celtics history as family property. Loyalty attaches to the green, the banners and the parquet first and to players a distant second, which is exactly what a reset season needs.

pulse.teamMoment: The Tatum-Brown era is over: after a 56-26 season ended in a 3-1 first-round collapse to Philadelphia, Brad Stevens traded Jaylen Brown to the 76ers for Paul George and picks and rebuilt around Jayson Tatum with Mitchell Robinson, Mike Conley and an extended Neemias Queta.
pulse.sentiment: Unsettled and skeptical: proud of Banner 18, bruised by the collapse, split on the Brown trade, and wary of George's age and contract after Tatum's father publicly criticized the roster and national free-agency grades panned the summer.

verifiedMoment: The Tatum-Brown era is over: after a 3-1 first-round collapse against Philadelphia, Brad Stevens traded Jaylen Brown to the 76ers for Paul George and picks and rebuilt the roster around Jayson Tatum.

scorecard.rationale: Boston pairs one of the league's most intense, heritage-driven fan bases and a deep, distinct civic and neighborhood culture with strong retail (the Garden, Newbury, Concepts, regional outlets), but the opportunity is capped this season by roster doubt and by rival brands' home-turf claims.

headline: Sell Brooklyn the city, not New York's other team: 112 codes, civic gilt and drops co-authored block by block.

archetype.name: The Borough Separatists
archetype.description: An outnumbered, style-literate tribe that treats the Nets as proof Brooklyn is its own city. Loyalty is to the borough first and the roster third, so it survives losing but punishes anything that reads as Manhattan, tourist or transplant.

pulse.teamMoment: A development year after a 20-62 season: No. 6 pick Mikel Brown Jr. and Egor Demin lead a very young roster beside veteran scorers Julius Randle and Michael Porter Jr. and new guard Keon Ellis, under newly extended Jordi Fernandez, with no opening-night or Christmas Day game.
pulse.sentiment: Patient, wry and mildly hopeful about the kids, and defiant about being Brooklyn while the defending-champion Knicks own the city's attention.

verifiedMoment: The Nets are still rebuilding, but with more veteran scoring: Julius Randle returns to New York alongside Michael Porter Jr., and No. 6 pick Mikel Brown Jr. leads a very young roster under a newly extended Jordi Fernandez.

scorecard.rationale: Brooklyn's culture is among the deepest and most designable in the league, but the Nets' fandom is thin after 20-62 in a Knicks title year and most partners and doors are unchecked. The opportunity rests on the borough mark selling without wins, and is conditional on local co-authorship and a 2027 build rather than this season.

opportunities.summary: This season's only real product lane: screen-printed tees, crewnecks and print-on-demand 112 ZIP numerals in black and bone, speaking as the City of Brooklyn, launched around the Nov. 3 anniversary and the start of the 15th Brooklyn season.

archetype.name: The Six-Banner Congregation
archetype.description: A multigenerational, all-sides faith in the 1991-98 Bulls that keeps buying through losing seasons but greets every rebuild promise with South Side and West Side sarcasm. It is loyal to the banners and the red-and-black, while the roster has to earn its place.

pulse.teamMoment: Year one of a new regime: Billy Donovan stepped down, Tiago Splitter took over as coach and EVP Bryson Graham is building a size-first 'SLAP' roster around Josh Giddey, Matas Buzelis and No. 4 pick Caleb Wilson, with Norman Powell and Nic Claxton added. The Bulls are coming off 31-51, are rated low in power rankings and have no opening-night or Christmas Day game; their early national stage is Emirates NBA Cup East Group C against Boston, Atlanta, Charlotte and Washington.
pulse.sentiment: Guarded hope wrapped in ownership fatigue: fans like the draft and Wilson's First Team All-Summer League debut but have learned to mock hype and wait for proof.

verifiedMoment: A new regime in Chicago: Billy Donovan stepped down, Tiago Splitter took over as coach and new EVP Bryson Graham is building for 'SLAP' (size, length, athleticism, physicality) around Josh Giddey, Matas Buzelis and No. 4 pick Caleb Wilson.

scorecard.rationale: Chicago is one of the league's deepest design cultures and a global heritage retail engine with a full flagship, arena, boutique and suburban-mall network. Fan intensity scores high on legacy but is held back by a 31-51 rebuild and ownership fatigue, so the near-term upside is in civic and outerwear product, mostly in the 2027-28 cycle, more than in current-player demand.

headline: Indiana is where the game lives: Hinkle week, 92 county numbers and the Avenue, worn in Pacers navy and gold.

archetype.name: The Keepers of the Gym
archetype.description: Fans raised on a single-class state tournament that ran until 1997, county gyms that out-seat their towns, and Hinkle's 1928 barrel vault. They reward effort over flash and wear navy and gold as Pacers loyalty that travels from Mass Ave to New Castle.

pulse.teamMoment: Tyrese Haliburton is back from the Achilles tear he suffered in Game 7 of the 2025 Finals and rejoins Siakam, Nembhard, Nesmith, McConnell and deadline pickup Ivica Zubac under Rick Carlisle after a 19-63 season, with Kelly Oubre Jr., Larry Nance Jr. and two-way Purdue guard Braden Smith added. Indiana hosts the 76ers on the Oct 30 opening Cup Night and has no opening-night or Christmas Day game.
pulse.sentiment: Cautiously hopeful and protective: fans expect a bounce-back toward contention but remember how fast the 2025 high ended, and they will punish anything that feels like hype or exploits the injury.

verifiedMoment: Tyrese Haliburton is back from the torn Achilles he suffered in Game 7 of the 2025 Finals ('I am healthy, ready to go,' Sept 28). He rejoins the Siakam-led 2025 Finals core, now with Ivica Zubac at center, after a lost 19-63 year.

scorecard.rationale: Indiana has one of the league's deepest basketball cultures and a one-off Hinkle Cup final in a comeback season, which lifts opportunity above average despite a small market. Retail sits below average: no destination flagship, a mall-first, value-led buyer, a star with a rival footwear deal and key cues that need third-party clearance.

pulse.teamMoment: After a 43-39, No. 10-seed season that ended in a 127-126 overtime Play-In loss at Charlotte, Miami traded Tyler Herro, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kel'el Ware and a haul of picks for Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bobby Portis, then signed Klay Thompson. Under Erik Spoelstra, a Giannis-Bam Adebayo frontcourt makes 2026-27 title-or-bust.
pulse.sentiment: Euphoric and demanding: the mood flipped from Play-In frustration to championship expectation, with real worry about depth after losing Herro, Jaquez, Ware and Norman Powell, and ESPN openly doubting the supporting cast.

verifiedMoment: Miami landed Giannis Antetokounmpo in one of the biggest trades in NBA history and added Klay Thompson. It is now a Giannis-Bam Adebayo contender on paper, and anything short of a deep run will read as failure.

scorecard.rationale: A Nike signature superstar arriving in a gateway shopping market, with some of the league's deepest multicultural design material and a real park-court culture, puts opportunity and culture near the top of the league. Retail is strong but sprawling and knockoff-pressured, and fandom peaks on White Hot playoff nights but is more front-running than the league's most loyal markets.

headline: With Giannis gone, the Bucks belong to Cream City again: sell the brick, the cold and the neighborhoods, not a new star.

archetype.name: The Working-City Loyalist
archetype.description: A statewide, blue-collar fan base that expects to be overlooked, values effort over glamour and stays loyal through a rebuild, but punishes anything that talks down to it or cashes in on its grief.

pulse.teamMoment: Milwaukee opens 2026-27 rebuilding after trading Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bobby Portis to Miami, with new coach Taylor Jenkins and a core of Tyler Herro, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kel'el Ware, Myles Turner, Kyle Kuzma and rookie Brayden Burries, coming off a 32-50 season.
pulse.sentiment: Grief and some anger over the trade, resignation about a long rebuild, and cautious curiosity about Herro and the rookies; nostalgia for 2021 is the safest emotion, and Jan 28 is circled by everyone.

verifiedMoment: Milwaukee faces its first season without Giannis Antetokounmpo in more than a decade, with a new coach in Taylor Jenkins. The Bucks are starting a long rebuild around Tyler Herro, the young pieces from the Miami trade and two lottery picks.

scorecard.rationale: Milwaukee has one of the league's most place-specific palettes and a deep working-class and neighborhood vernacular, but a small, value-minded market in a low-expectation rebuild, a thin sneaker scene and no Nike-owned door in the city keep opportunity average and retail below average. Fandom is loyal and statewide but at low heat until Jan 28.

headline: 53 years, then a ring: sell New York's title through its parks, counters and borough doors, not its skyline.

archetype.name: The Vindicated Lifers
archetype.description: A multigenerational, five-borough fan base that kept selling out the Mecca through 53 ringless years and now wants to say 'told you' in its own codes. It values grit, defense and heritage over flash and spots anything corporate or touristy from a block away.

pulse.teamMoment: Defending champions after a 53-29 season and a 16-3 playoff run capped by Brunson's Finals MVP and a 94-90 Game 5 clincher over San Antonio; the core is intact under the second apron, and the defense opens with ring night against LeBron James' and Jaylen Brown's 76ers on Oct 20.
pulse.sentiment: Euphoric and protective: fans are flush with the first title since 1973 and expect a real defense in a tougher East, with old ownership grievances quieter but not forgotten.

verifiedMoment: The defending champions: the Knicks won their first title since 1973, with Jalen Brunson as Finals MVP. They kept most of the roster under the second apron, and the defense starts with a ring night against LeBron James and Jaylen Brown's new-look 76ers.

scorecard.rationale: The league's biggest market defending its first title in 53 years, with the deepest homegrown basketball, music and art culture to design from. Scores are held down because it is also the most crowded, license-heavy market (MSG, MTA, Puma's Clyde, Fanatics, a locked 2026-27 City Edition), so Nike's real lanes are the AF1 Uptowns and Flax, Specter, the park circuit and the borough doors, all assuming rights and doors check out.

pulse.teamMoment: Orlando chose continuity: Jamahl Mosley was fired after a 45-37 season that ended with a Play-In escape and a first-round loss to No. 1 Detroit, Sean Sweeney arrived from San Antonio, and Vucevic is back beside Banchero, Wagner and Bane. The open questions are Wagner's health after 34 games and three ball-dominant stars with no true point guard.
pulse.sentiment: Cautiously hopeful but impatient: fans like the core and Vucevic's return, but the mood has moved from 'rebuild' to 'prove it', and nobody wants hype before results.

verifiedMoment: Orlando chose continuity over a splash: it fired Jamahl Mosley, hired Spurs defensive architect Sean Sweeney and is betting he can make the Banchero-Wagner-Bane trio work. Vucevic is back for his second Magic stint.

scorecard.rationale: Opportunity sits above average because Nike owns the Penny-pinstripe nostalgia outright and Central Florida's Puerto Rican and tourist audiences are large, but no national-TV stage, modest local incomes and a prove-it season cap it. Culture is deep but under-designed (Eatonville, Parramore, OBT signage, Boricua Orlando), retail is outlet-heavy with a thin taste layer, and fandom is loyal but playoff-gated in a transplant market.

pulse.teamMoment: After a 45-37 Play-In season, a comeback from 3-1 down against No. 2 Boston and a second-round sweep by the eventual champion Knicks, Philly traded Paul George for Jaylen Brown and signed LeBron James to join Embiid, Maxey and Edgecombe. Title odds moved to about +1000, and Nick Nurse is under maximum pressure.
pulse.sentiment: Giddy but braced. The city knows Embiid's availability, LeBron turning 42 in December and the fresh Knicks wound decide the year, and it will judge both new stars on effort, not reputation.

verifiedMoment: Philadelphia had the summer's biggest swing: Jaylen Brown arrived by trade from Boston and LeBron James signed as a free agent, joining Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and VJ Edgecombe. The questions are health and age, and Nick Nurse is under maximum pressure.

scorecard.rationale: A title-contending superteam with Nike's LeBron, a Specter season and a new arena coming to the Spectrum site make this one of the league's biggest 2026-27 openings, and few markets offer as deep a culture to design from. Retail is broad but the taste-setting independents are thin since Ubiq closed and the throwback lane belongs to Mitchell & Ness, and fan intensity is elite but shares the winter with the Eagles.

headline: Oakland is the soul, San Francisco the address: win the Bay on the bridge between them, in gear built for fog.

archetype.name: The Dynasty Diaspora
archetype.description: A fan base forged in 40 lean Oakland years and spoiled by four titles, now spread across The Town, The City and the 408. It is loyal to Curry, Draymond and Kerr more than to an arena, and it is nostalgic for Oracle in a building that never had Oracle's soul.

pulse.teamMoment: Curry's aging core ran it back after a 37-45 season, a play-in win over the Clippers and a 111-96 loss at Phoenix: the Warriors chased Giannis and Anthony Davis without a deal, re-signed Porzingis, Horford, Melton and Gary Payton II, added Niang and Brandon Williams, drafted Yaxel Lendeborg at No. 11, and have Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody recovering from injury.

verifiedMoment: Stephen Curry's aging core ran it back after failing to land another star (the Warriors explored Giannis and Anthony Davis). Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody are still recovering from injuries.

scorecard.rationale: Culture is near the top (two cities, three subcultural lineages, huge Asian American communities), but opportunity is held to the low 70s by a 40.5 win total, injured Butler and Moody, an open Curry deal and a winter-only window. scorecard.rationale: The NBA's most mythologized brand is resetting its jersey wall in a vast, multilingual market with design traditions (South Central signage, Chicano lettering and serigraphs, lowriders, Kobe murals, immigrant food color) few cities can match, and every retail tier from Fairfax to Citadel is already there. headline: Nike wins Minnesota in the skyway season: layers, the North Star and community-led product, not the stars' shoes.

archetype.description: A polite but stubborn statewide fan base that wears its scars (Garnett's exit, the drought, a former Wolf winning a title in New York) and wants belief, not victory laps. It dresses for wind chill below zero and reps area codes and neighborhoods before skylines.

verifiedMoment: Minnesota doubled down on Anthony Edwards by trading for LaMelo Ball, creating one of the league's most electric backcourts. The Wolves have 27 national TV games and host OKC on Christmas.

scorecard.rationale: Minnesota has one of the league's deepest design vernaculars (the Minneapolis Sound, Mill City, winter craft and strong Somali, Hmong, Native and Northside scenes) and a newly loud Edwards-Ball fan base. pulse.teamMoment: New coach Jamahl Mosley inherits Zion Williamson, breakout scorer Trey Murphy III (21.5 ppg, kept through June trade rumors) and second-year Derik Queen and Jeremiah Fears after a 26-56 season and a quiet offseason under Joe Dumars. The team is not on the opening-night or Christmas slates; NBA Cup West Group B (OKC, MIN, LAC, MEM), opening Oct 30 at the Clippers, is the early-season stage.

verifiedMoment: New coach Jamahl Mosley inherits Zion Williamson, breakout Trey Murphy III and young Derik Queen and Jeremiah Fears after a quiet offseason with no first-round pick.

scorecard.rationale: Few NBA cities have a deeper or more design-ready local culture, and its calendar lines up with the season. But retail is thin (few destination sneaker doors, a modest arena store, a price-conscious core), and Pelicans fandom is small, Saints-first and weary after 26-56. The opportunity sits just below average, held up by city-first product that can sell regardless of the standings.

headline: Oklahoma's only big-league team: sell its sky and red dirt in Thunder blue, statewide and under $100.

archetype.name: The One-Team State
archetype.description: A whole state that adopted a franchise in 2008 and now treats a champion as its civic uniform. Loud, loyal, value-minded and allergic to flash that the team has not earned.

pulse.teamMoment: Back-to-back MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's Thunder went 64-18 and are 2026-27 co-title favorites (BetMGM win total 60.5) after San Antonio beat them 4-3 in the West finals. Luguentz Dort, Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins were traded, Aday Mara arrived at No. 12, and Sam Presti says he won't cut a payroll heading toward about $260M.
pulse.sentiment: Confident but stung. Fans expect a title, see the Oct 20 opener at San Antonio as a grudge match, and trust Presti and Daigneault's patient build even as familiar rotation players leave.

verifiedMoment: Back-to-back MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's Thunder are 2026-27 co-title favorites after a seven-game West finals loss to San Antonio ended their title defense. Payroll is rising toward about $260M, and Sam Presti says he won't cut to avoid it.

scorecard.rationale: A champion that is the only big-league team in an entire state gives OKC near-top fan intensity and a large statewide opportunity for a small metro, with distinct red-dirt, sky, Route 66 and community stories to design from. Retail lags: a car-based, value-minded metro with no Nike community door and a small sneaker scene.

archetype.name: The Insider Loyalist
archetype.description: A fan base that stayed through 814 sellouts, the Jail Blazers and Lillard's exit and return, and that reads every jersey for fabric, fit and who designed it because it lives next door to Beaverton. pulse.teamMoment: New owner Tom Dundon's Blazers add Ja Morant (acquired from Memphis on June 29) to a backcourt with Damian Lillard, back from a torn Achilles, under first-year coach Micah Nori, after a 42-40 season that ended 4-1 to San Antonio in the first round. Oregon, Multnomah County and Portland have committed $586M toward Moda Center upgrades, but the lease is still unsigned.
pulse.sentiment: Hopeful but guarded: emotional about Lillard back in a Blazers uniform after a lost season, split on Morant's talent versus his 2023 suspensions, debating whether Nori brings one of them off the bench, and relieved the team is staying while wary of an owner who says he won't pay for the renovation.

verifiedMoment: New owner Tom Dundon's Blazers add Ja Morant to a backcourt with Damian Lillard, back from a torn Achilles, under first-year coach Micah Nori. The Moda Center renovation lease is still being negotiated.

scorecard.rationale: A once-only heritage year, an empty City Edition slot and a deep roster in Nike's own hometown make the opportunity large, and Albina, Rip City broadcast lore, maker craft and supporter culture give unusually deep design material. Retail lags because the metro has few public Nike doors, a thinned downtown and a Rose Quarter retail desert, and this season's lead times limit what can ship before February; fandom is intense and statewide but guarded about Morant and the owner.

archetype.name: The Keepers
archetype.description: A fan base that personally rescued its team and now treats every home game as civic duty. It forgives losing but not condescension, and it punishes anything that reads as Bay Area, Lakers or outsider.

pulse.teamMoment: A youth movement after a 22-60 season and a lost lottery tiebreak: No. 7 pick Darius Acuff Jr. joins Domantas Sabonis, Zach LaVine and Malik Monk under Doug Christie in his second full season, with no opening-night or Christmas Day game and a Cup group with the Spurs, Lakers, Warriors and Trail Blazers.

verifiedMoment: A youth movement led by No. 7 pick Darius Acuff Jr. around holdovers Domantas Sabonis, Zach LaVine and Malik Monk. Sacramento is widely projected near the bottom of the West.

scorecard.rationale: Fan loyalty is well above league average because the city saved the team and treats attendance as civic duty, and the Tower Bridge, Beam and neighborhood scenes give real design material. A rebuild year, a value-leaning Valley and the lack of a full-price Nike door or a dense boutique scene hold the opportunity and retail readiness near or below average.
